title: Kidney stones: four families
label: Original Study Hub teaching illustration, not a patient photograph. Stone and crystal appearances vary.
prompt:
Create one ORIGINAL illustrated nursing-study infographic, portrait 1024x1536, highly polished and clinically careful. Caroline likes dark jewel tones: sapphire, emerald, amethyst, burgundy, gold. Use a restrained abstract Klimt-inspired gold medical mosaic border; cream high-contrast type, large headings, generous spacing. Rich anatomically plausible stone illustrations with meaningful memory characters, not generic icon-only shapes. Readable 4-card 2-by-2 layout. No logos.

TITLE: "KIDNEY STONES"
SUBTITLE: "4 families • different causes and care"
Small important line: "Illustrative appearances vary. Lab stone analysis confirms the type."
Small kidney-and-ureter anatomical cutaway near title showing a stone in renal collecting system.

Each card has one large whole-stone illustration clearly labeled "Stone example", a separate magnifying-circle inset explicitly labeled "Urine crystals", a brief memory cue scene and clinical text. Distinguish stone appearance from crystals; never imply a passed stone has the exact microscopic crystal outline.

CARD 1 emerald, title "CALCIUM".
Whole-stone examples: rough irregular brown calcium oxalate stone and smaller pale cream calcium phosphate stone, separately labeled.
Microscopy inset: a translucent envelope-shaped calcium oxalate DIHYDRATE crystal plus dumbbell MONOHYDRATE crystal, labels "Oxalate: envelope or dumbbell".
Text:
"Most common family"
"Oxalate: common; variable urine pH"
"Phosphate: favors alkaline urine"
"Keep normal food calcium; reduce sodium."
"Limit excess oxalate when indicated."
Memory cue: cheerful calcium courier holds an ENVELOPE beside a milk carton WITH a meal; label "Calcium courier: keep food calcium."

CARD 2 sapphire, title "URIC ACID".
Stone example: smooth-to-granular orange-yellow rounded stone.
Microscopy inset: amber rhomboid/diamond crystals, label "Rhomboids / rosettes".
Text:
"Favors acidic urine"
"Purines and gout may contribute"
"Reduce excess animal protein."
"Prescribed urine alkalinization."
Memory cue a tiny diamond-shaped amber crystal beside a clearly labeled "ACID" laboratory flask, not food or drink; label "Uric acid = acid."

CARD 3 burgundy, title "STRUVITE".
Stone example: branching pale tan STAGHORN calculus shaped to the renal pelvis and calyces, with a faint kidney silhouette behind it, label "May form a staghorn".
Microscopy inset: translucent rectangular prism with beveled ends (coffin lid), label "Coffin-lid crystals".
Text:
"Urease-producing UTI • alkaline urine"
"Often needs stone removal + antibiotics."
"Not every staghorn is struvite."
Memory cue: tiny stag with branching antlers and recognizable cartoon bacteria, label "Struvite = STAG + infection."

CARD 4 amethyst, title "CYSTINE".
Stone example: waxy-looking pale yellow rounded stone.
Microscopy inset: multiple flat, colorless SIX-sided hexagonal crystals, label "Hexagonal crystals".
Text:
"Inherited cystinuria"
"Cystine leaks into urine"
"Fluids + lower sodium."
"Prescribed urine alkalinization."
Memory cue: family crest with DNA ribbon and SIX-sided shield; label "Cystine = six sides + family."

BOTTOM NURSING STRIP with strainer, specimen container, water and pain-assessment icons:
"STRAIN • SAVE • ASSESS"
"Strain urine; save stones for analysis. Monitor pain, output and infection."
"Fluids follow the individual plan—do not force fluids through obstruction."
Strong red-gold PRIORITY box: "FEVER + BLOCKED URINE = URGENT"
"Possible infected obstruction: prompt assessment and drainage may be needed."
Small footer "Original Study Hub memory illustration • Sources: NIDDK; Frazier & Huppmann (2021); EAU Urolithiasis Guideline."
Keep all text legible; ensure every shape has correct anatomy and leader lines. Educational schematic, not a patient photograph.
